column3: Priestly service is expressed in the singular rather than “as priests.”
Describes the craftsmen as “wise of heart,” retaining the heart image rather than simply “skilled craftsmen.”
The final priestly service phrase is singular rather than “they may serve Me as priests.”
Uses “take” for the materials rather than “use.”
Calls it the work of a skilled designer rather than specifying embroidery.
Names two ends rather than two corners.
“The second stone” retains the ordinal rather than “the other.”
Repeats the making instruction three times: for the breastpiece, its correspondence to the ephod, and its materials.
Names the two ends of the breastpiece rather than two corners.
Names the ends of the breastpiece rather than the corners.
Retains “the two ends of the two cords,” without explicitly adding “other.”
Does not explicitly add “more” to the rings or “other” to the ends.
Does not explicitly add “additional” to the rings.
People bind the breastpiece by its rings; the breastpiece remains the object rather than making its rings the subject of a passive clause.
